questions.question: The power to summon each House of Parliament is vested with the:
questions.solution:
The **power** to **summon** both the Houses of Parliament i.e. Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha is vested with the __**President**__ of India under Article 85(1) of the Indian Constitution.

 
• **Article 85(1)** empowers the President to summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit.
 
• **Budget**, **Monsoon**, and **Winter Sessions**, are held in a calendar year.
 
• The President may also, from time to time
 
 
• Prorogue the houses
 
• dissolve the house of the people.
 
 
 
• **Vice President** is the **Chairman** of the Council of States/Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: The Netravati River flows through which of the following cities?

questions.question: Which of the following may be classified as a 'Pigouvian tax'?
questions.solution:
**__Carbon tax__** can be classified as a **__Pigouvian tax.__**

 
• A **Pigouvian tax** can be defined as tax which is assessed against the private individuals or businesses for engaging in the activities that can create **adverse side effects for the society**.
 
• Its popular example is a tax on pollution. Pollution from an industrial plant can create a negative side effect.
 
• Pigouvian taxes were named after economist, Arthur Pigou.
 
• **Long term capital gain tax** is a tax levied on the sale of an asset that generates profit in the long term.
 
• Income Tax is levied on the income of an individual.

questions.question: According to the Demographic Transition Theory, the third stage in a demographic cycle is marked by:
questions.solution:
According to the **__Demographic Transition Theory__**, the third stage in a demographic cycle is marked by__ **low fertility low mortality**__

 
• **Demographic transition theory **is used to** predict the future population of any area. **
;The population of any region changes from** high births and high deaths to lower births and lower deaths.**
 
• The **first stage** has a **high mortality** and **high fertility rate**.
 
• **Fertility** remains high at the beginning of the second stage but then it **starts to decline**. This leads to a **reduced mortality rate**.
 
• In the last stage, which is the **third stage** in the cycle, both **fertility and mortality decline** considerably.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ionosphere is NOT correct?

options.text: Radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
It is ionized by solar and cosmic radiation.
It is located immediately above the stratopause.

questions.solution:
The **Ionosphere** is the ionized part of Earth's upper atmosphere, which extends from about **__60 km to 1,000 km__** altitude.

 
• The ionosphere is a very active part of the atmosphere, and it grows and shrinks depending on the energy it absorbs from the Sun.
 
• It contains charged particles and is ionized by solar radiation.
 
• The ionosphere is a region that includes the thermosphere and parts of the **mesosphere** and **exosphere**.

questions.question: What would you call the area under the curve of a velocity-time graph included between itself and two time ordinates?
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

__
 
• **Displacement (X):** The change in the position of an object is called displacement.

 
 
• **Displacement** is a **one-dimensional quantity** representing the smallest separation between two defined points.
 
• The standard unit of displacement in the International System of Units (SI) is the meter (m).
 
 
 
• 
 
**Velocity (V)**: The rate of change of displacement is called velocity. It is a vector quantity. 

 
 
• 
 
The SI unit of velocity is called m/s and the CGS unit is cm/s.

 
 
• 
 
The slope of the displacement-time graph gives the velocity.

 
 
 

Instantaneous velocity ( V ) = frac{{dx}}{{dt}}

V = frac{{dx}}{{dt}}

Hence dx = V dt 

Displacement ( X ) = mathop smallint nolimits{ₓ₁}{x_²} dx = mathop smallint nolimits{ₜ₁}{t_²} V dt

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/117de6828386582e21e5df8e4e7e28dd2b37290705d79d8945a8f308336fce56.png] 

 
• Thus the **area under the velocity-time graph gives the displacement**. Similarly, the area under-speed time graph gives the total distance travelled.

**EXPLANATION**__:

 
• The **area under a velocity-time graph is a representation of the displacement**. So option 2 is correct.
 
• The rate of change of distance is called **speed**.

questions.question: Researchers from the UK and India have developed a hand-washing robot, who has been named:

questions.question: In the context of Overseas Citizens of India (OCI), which of the following statements is **NOT **correct?

options.text: A foreign national those who or either of whose parents or grandparents or great grandparents is or had been a citizen of Pakistan or Bangladesh, is not eleigible for it.
An OCI is granted multiple entry visa for a period of ten years only.
An OCI is allowed to undertake all activities except research work for which special permission is required.
Any foreign national who was eligible to become a citizen of India on 26.01.1950 is eligible for it.

questions.solution:
The Government of India has granted **multiple entry visas** for an __**indefinite period**__ to **Overseas Citizens of India (OCI)**.

 
• The government of India launched the ‘**Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) Scheme**’ by amending the Citizenship Act, 1955 in **2005**.
 
• The Government of India **discontinued the Person of Indian Origin (PIO) card** and **merged** it with the **OCI card**.
 
• They **do not have the Right to Vote**.
 
• An OCI is an **immigration status** given to a foreign citizen of Indian origin to **live and work in India** indefinitely.
 
• Anyone who is applying for OCI card should **hold a valid Passport** of another country.
 
• Benefits for OCI cardholders include lifelong Visa to visit India multiple times, but **special permission needed for research work in India.**
 
• However, Individuals having parents/grandparents with **Pakistani citizenship OR Bangladeshi citizenship** **cannot apply for OCI**.

questions.question: Which of the following provisions of the Indian Constitution is correctly paired with the article pertaining to it?

options.text: Protection of life and personal liberty - Article 21
Prohibition of traffic in human beings - Article 24
Prohibition of employment of any child below fourteen years of age in any factory or mine - Article 23

questions.solution:
The Fundamental Rights have been described in **Articles 12-35**, **Part III **of the Indian Constitution.

 
• **Right to Life and Personal Liberty** is a right enshrined in **Article 21** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This right **cannot be curtailed** even during the **National Emergency (Article 359)**.
 
• Other rights within the ambit of Article 21 includes the recently upheld **Right to Privacy** by the Supreme Court in the **Puttuswamy Case**.
 
• **Prohibition of traffic in human beings** is enshrined in **Article 23** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Right to education is enshrined in **Article 21A** which was a result of the 86th Amendment 2002 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It provides for **free and compulsory **education until the **age of 14** for all children.
 
• **Prohibition of employment** **of any child below fourteen years of age in any factory or mine** is enshrined in **Article 24** of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: In the Canada Deuterium Uranium (CANDU) reactor, a natural uranium-fuelled reactor, the function of moderator and coolant is performed by:
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

Nuclear reactor:

__
 
• It is a device in which a nuclear reaction is initiated, maintained, and controlled.
 
• It works on the principle of controlled chain reaction and provides energy at a constant rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4ba71a5536aeaa05350d075668e0a630dec8d4941e5527ebb122ccfc34ee755a.png] 

EXPLANATION__:

 
• The function of the moderator and coolant in the Canada Deuterium Uranium (CANDU) reactor is performed by heavy water
 
• The moderator's function is to slow down the fast-moving secondary neutrons produced during the fission. T
 
• The material of the moderator should be light and it should not absorb neutrons.
 
• Usually, heavy water, graphite, deuterium, and paraffin, etc. can act as moderators.
 
• The heat released by fission in nuclear reactors must be captured and transferred for use in electricity generation.
 
• To this end, reactors use coolants that remove heat from the core where the fuel is processed and carry it to electrical generators. 
 
• Coolants also serve to maintain manageable pressures within the core.

• Ocean currents have influences of **Coriolis force, frictional force, and heating effect of the sun.**
 
• The sun heats water at the surface of the ocean which will evaporate and increase the concentration of salt and water will become dense and settle down hence whose place is taken by less dense water which leads to Ocean currents
 
• Wind forces also play a major role to influence ocean currents.

questions.question: Once a satellite has been launched into orbit, the only force governing its motion is the force of ______.
questions.solution:
**__CONCEPT:__**

__
 
• A **satellite **is an object that has been placed into the orbit. This is also known as artificial satellite.
 
• There are natural satellite also. eg. Moon
 
• The **force of elasticity** occurs as a deformed object (think spring) tries to return to its original shape. The force always acts in a direction that will return it to its original shape.
 
• **Friction **is the force which resist the relative motion between solid surfaces, fluid layers, etc. **sliding against each other**.
 
• **Gravity **is an universal force that acts over large distances between any two masses.
 
• Due to Gravity a planet or other body draws objects toward its center.

**EXPLANATION:**__

 
• Satellites orbits around the planet because they have enough speed that is fast enough to defeat the downward pull of gravity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2bfc1a1e97941b50ed0dfe777e5c1ca2167569036939c10876afd076ad40252.png] 

 
• A satellite revolves in its orbit and **balance two factors: its velocity** (the speed it takes to travel in a straight line) **and the gravity force **that Earth has on it.
 
• So The correct answer is **option**** 1 **i.e**. gravity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/49db1e88466c4075382b1073285f91a9ab0332e48bb5db4e537f337fc9ab0472.png] 

 
• Due to no loss in energy of satellite while orbiting, **fuel is not used for energy to the satellite**. While fuel is required in the form of kinetic energy or speed of the satellite to put it in an orbit around the planet.

questions.question: Which one of the following attributes is NOT true for uniform circular motion?

options.text: The distance is always equal to the displacement
Velocity is always perpendicular to the radius of the circle
The speed of the body remains constant
The velocity of the body is continuously changing

questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• In a uniform circular motion, a body is experiencing a force in the inward direction

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb04ec9797808e6bb147499ecb1af0e7ec231e2440591959e86e91ab056c2923.png] 

 
• Acceleration of the body is non-zero and has magnitude v2/r
 
• For a uniform circular motion, **Speed of object remains constant.**
 
• Whereas the velocity keeps on changing because the direction of **velocity is changing continuously** and it is **perpendicular to radius of the circle.**
 
• >Distance:__
 __
 
• The length of the actual path covered by a moving object in a given time.
 
• It is a scalar quantity.
 
• It is always positive.
 
• The unit of distance is a meter (m).
 
 
 
• >Displacement:__
 __
 
• It is the shortest distance covered by a body in a definite direction.
 
• It is a vector quantity.
 
• It can be positive, Negative or Zero.
 
 

Explanation:__

 
• As explained above **the distance is not always equal to the displacement** in a uniform circular motion.
 
• In a uniform circular motion, an object moves along a circular path with uniform speed.
 
• Due to a circular path travelled the distance will be greater than zero but the **displacement can or cannot be zero.**
 
• The displacement is In UCM is called as **angular displacement.**
 
• Velocity is always perpendicular to the radius.
